title: Creating Work Types

children:
A work type is a general subset of a work group, based on processing 
 needs or characteristics. For example, batch 
 picking could be a work type of the larger group,     picking. 
 In this example, the type identifies all picking work that is ideally 
 processed in batch mode. Many common work types, such as batch picking 
 and order picking, are provided with the system. However, you can create 
 additional work types to support your business needs. Later, you can define 
 work processing rules based on work types on the Work Profile Window.

Use the Work 
 Type Field to name your new work type.
Use the Description Field to provide a text description for your work type.

Use the Labor 
 Type Field to describe the type of labor management record you 
 want this work type to generate.
Use the Labor Group Field to identify a group of users that perform similar work related functions.

Use the Transaction 
 Count Description to identify the text for a custom field that 
 will appear on the Manual Labor Entry Screen. This text label will also have a numeric field associated 
 with it. For example, suppose you have a work type defined for "Sweeping 
 Floors," which the warehouse janitor is supposed to track their time 
 with on the Manual Labor Entry Screen. If the Transaction Count Description 
 Field has a value such as "Aisles Swept?, the user then could indicate 
 on the Manual Labor Entry Screen how much work they finished during a 
 certain time period.

Use the Work 
 Group Field to associate your work type with the appropriate work 
 group.

Use the Default 
 Priority Field to determine the priority assigned to all work units 
 for this work type. A user's work profile record includes a From Assignment 
 value. This value determines how the system will sort work for that employee. 
 If the From Assignment Field includes a priority sort, such as the Priority/Location/FIFO 
 value, the system will reference the value defined here.

NOTE: The priority value is only assigned if the work is performed 
 in system directed mode, via an RF device. If you are processing work 
 via a full screen (non-RF), the system cannot assign based on priority 
 (since you manually assign the work).

Use the Pick 
 Management Active Checkbox to indicate if the system will display 
 this work type on the Picking Management processing windows. Only work 
 types that have this checkbox selected will be available to be picked 
 from. Both this checkbox and the From Work Zone on the work instruction 
 must have a value to be eligible for picking from these windows.

Press OK. 
 The system will save your record.
